tools.name: whiteboard_session_get_instructions
tools.description:
Load Whiteboard's guide before you create or edit a Whiteboard session. A Whiteboard session is a code walkthrough document that the user reads in a Whiteboard panel tab on the calling bb thread. When the user asks for a Whiteboard or to use Whiteboard (for example to review a branch, a change or a pull request, or to explain a system in Whiteboard), call this first and follow what it returns.

TOPICS

- Omit `topic` (or pass "authoring") for the authoring workflow, document structure and component shapes. Read it before `whiteboard_session_create` or your first `whiteboard_session_edit`.
- "file-lenses": how to group a session's changes into Diff-view lenses with `whiteboard_session_lens_edit`. Point the agent that writes lenses to it.

Returns the guide as Markdown.

RULES FOR EVERY WHITEBOARD TOOL

- Read `whiteboard_session_capabilities` before authoring, and generate software maps only when it reports `softwareMapEnabled: true`.
- `whiteboard_session_create` opens the new session as a tab in the calling thread; call `whiteboard_session_open` only to show an existing session.
- Read and write Whiteboard data only through these tools, never through its files or database.
- Every write takes a `commandId` UUID: a fresh one for each operation, and the same one with identical input when you retry after a lost response.

tools.name: whiteboard_status
tools.description:
Report which Whiteboard plugin version and bb instance serve this call. Use it when the user asks which Whiteboard version is running, or to include the version in a bug report. To check what a session can do before authoring, use `whiteboard_session_capabilities`.

Returns JSON: `appVersion` (the Whiteboard plugin version), `channel` ("bb-plugin"), `instanceId` (the bb server's public app URL, or null when none is configured), and `desktopAvailable` (true when called from a bb thread, where sessions open as panel tabs). In bb, `key` is always "stable" and `checkout`, `cliVersion`, `url` and `home` are always null.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_capabilities
tools.description:
Check what Whiteboard can do for this call before you author a session or draw on the scratchpad. Returns `desktopAvailable` (true when called from a bb thread, so sessions can open there as panel tabs), `softwareMapEnabled` (the Software Map setting), and `scratchpadEnabled` (the Scratchpad setting).

Generate software maps only when `softwareMapEnabled` is true. Uploading an existing map with `whiteboard_session_upload` works either way.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_activity
tools.description:
Claim a Whiteboard session for writing and show the user what you are working on. Begin a lease before your first write, pass its `leaseId` on every write in that scope, and end it when the work is finished.

- `scope` "document" (default) covers `whiteboard_session_edit`, `whiteboard_session_set_target`, `whiteboard_session_repin`, `whiteboard_session_rename`, `whiteboard_session_restore` and `whiteboard_session_delete`; "lenses" covers `whiteboard_session_lens_edit`. Each scope has its own lease, so one agent can write lenses while another writes the document.
- `begin` with a fresh UUID `leaseId`. While another agent's lease holds the scope, `begin` and writes without that lease are refused; wait for it to end or expire.
- `renew` during long reads or pauses; accepted writes that carry the `leaseId` renew it too. A lease expires after 3 minutes without either; then begin a new lease and reread the session before editing.
- `end` when finished. It saves no version, and repeating it is harmless.

`focus` (`description`, optional `targetId`, which names a lens in the lenses scope) shows the reader what you are working on; omit it to keep the current focus, or pass null to clear it.

Returns `workingCount`, `expiresAt`, and the live `scopes` and `focuses`. The panel shows an agent working while any lease is live and treats a session with content and no live lease as ready to read, so end your lease only when you are done.

scope.description: What the lease covers. Default "document": whiteboard_session_edit and every other session write except lens edits. "lenses": whiteboard_session_lens_edit only.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_delete
tools.description:
Permanently delete a Whiteboard session and all its versions. Delete only when the user asks; to hide a session from Whiteboard Home instead, use `whiteboard_session_attention` with action "dismiss". The scratchpad cannot be deleted.

Pass a fresh UUID `commandId` and your document `leaseId` from `whiteboard_session_activity`; while another agent holds that lease, the delete is refused. Deletion cannot be undone. A retry after a lost response fails with a not-found error saying the command's session was deleted, which confirms the deletion.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_attention
tools.description:
Change how a Whiteboard session appears on Whiteboard Home, without changing its content or creating a version. `action` "dismiss" moves it to the dismissed group, "restore" brings it back, and "view" records that the user has seen it (`viewedAt`). Use it when the user asks to dismiss, restore or mark a session as viewed. The scratchpad cannot be dismissed or marked.

Pass a fresh UUID `commandId`; no lease is needed. After a lost response, retry with the same `commandId` and identical input.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_create
tools.description:
Create a Whiteboard session for the code or change the user wants explained, and open it as a tab in the calling bb thread. Read `whiteboard_session_get_instructions` first, and register the checkout with `whiteboard_session_register_repository` to get its `repositoryId` (for a pull request, a checkout of the PR's GitHub repository).

SOURCES

- "target" (the usual choice): `title` and a `target`. A worktree target shows the checkout's saved working files and follows them; omitted `base` compares against its current commit. A commits target shows fixed commits; omitted `base` shows `head` with no diff, so pass the parent to show what a commit introduced. Revisions resolve to commit IDs when the command is accepted.
- "pull-request": `pullRequestUrl` alone. The PR is fetched into a registered checkout (`repositoryId` picks one), pinned at its head and GitHub's diff base, and titled from the PR unless you pass `title`.
- "pins": `title` and full commit `pins` from `whiteboard_session_resolve_pins`. Prefer "target".
- "scratchpad" always fails: Whiteboard makes each thread's scratchpad itself. Write to it with `sessionId: "scratchpad"`.

When a session for `pullRequestUrl` already exists, it is returned instead (`created: false`) without your title or target; read its `note`. If `headMoved`, move it with `whiteboard_session_set_target`; `ownedBy` means another agent holds its lease. Pass `reuseExisting: false` to create a separate session.

Returns `sessionId`, `version`, and `session` (its `whiteboard_session_list` row, with resolved commits and `repositoryPath`), so you can call `whiteboard_session_diff` next without another read. The session opens in the calling thread unless you pass `open: false`; `opened` and any `openError` report that, and a failed open does not undo the create. Then begin a document lease with `whiteboard_session_activity`.

Pass a fresh UUID `commandId`. After a lost response, retry with the same `commandId` and identical input to get the original result.

reuseExisting.description: Default true: return the existing Whiteboard session for pullRequestUrl instead of creating one. false creates a separate session.

repositoryId.description: The registered checkout to fetch the PR into. Default: the existing session's checkout, else the first registered checkout with a GitHub remote for the PR's repository.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_set_target
tools.description:
Move an existing Whiteboard session to a new target, such as a PR's new head or a different base, keeping its document and component IDs. Use it to update a Whiteboard for newer code or after a create reports `headMoved`; use `whiteboard_session_repin` only to change the session's PR.

`target` takes the shapes `whiteboard_session_create` accepts and resolves to commit IDs when the command is accepted. Moving to another repository detaches the session's PR. Earlier versions keep their own source.

Returns `warnings` naming the source references and resources to recheck. Read the change since the old target, then fix them with `whiteboard_session_edit`.

Pass a fresh UUID `commandId` and your document `leaseId` from `whiteboard_session_activity`. After a lost response, retry with the same `commandId` and identical input. The scratchpad has no target.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_edit
tools.description:
Write one component of a Whiteboard session's document: add, change, move or remove a section, prose block, code peek or diagram. Use `whiteboard_session_lens_edit` for Diff-view lenses; this tool edits the document itself.

BEFORE CALLING

- Read `whiteboard_session_get_instructions` (default topic) for component fields and examples.
- Begin `whiteboard_session_activity` with a fresh UUID `leaseId` and document scope, then pass that same `leaseId` on every edit.
- Cite only ranges you have read with `whiteboard_session_source` or `whiteboard_session_file`. An edit is rejected when a new source range does not exist at its pins or a code peek's range is blank.

EDIT OPERATIONS

- `insert` adds `content`; `parentId` nests it, `afterId` places it, and omitted placement appends. On the scratchpad, omitted placement inserts at the top: use `afterId` to order multiple blocks.
- `update` patches the target's own fields through `changes`; `null` removes an optional field. `replace` supplies a whole replacement block. `move` and `remove` address `targetId`.
- Insert a new diagram whole. Edit an existing diagram one node, edge, or step at a time. Insert a `flow_node`, `flow_edge`, or `step` with the diagram's ID as `parentId`; connect each added flow node to an existing node with `link`. Removing a flow node removes its edges.
- Replace a call-stack block to change its frames.

RETURNS AND RECOVERY
Accepted edits save immediately as a new version and return the component's durable ID as `targetId`, plus first-level child IDs in `children` for an insert or replace. Use those IDs for later edits to a section's children or a diagram's units, and repair any references named in `warnings`. Use a fresh UUID `commandId` for each operation; after a lost response, retry with the same ID and identical input. If an edit is refused because the session changed or your lease ended, reread it with `whiteboard_session_get`, begin a new lease if yours ended, and retry.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_lens_edit
tools.description:
Write one Diff-view lens: a titled group of a Whiteboard session's changed lines, shown on the Diffs page beside the document, never in it. Follow `whiteboard_session_get_instructions({topic:"file-lenses"})` for how to group a change; use `whiteboard_session_edit` for the document.

Begin `whiteboard_session_activity` with `scope: "lenses"` and pass its `leaseId`. The document lease does not cover lenses.

- `insert` adds a lens with `title` and `targets`, after lens `afterId` or at the end.
- `update` replaces only the `title` or `targets` you pass on lens `targetId`; `remove` deletes it.
- `targets` select changed lines by repository-relative paths or globs (`kind: "files"`) or by source ranges (`kind: "ranges"`).

Write one lens per call; each appears on the Diffs page as you write it. Returns the lens ID as `targetId` and `uncategorized`: the changed lines no lens selects yet, by file. Keep adding lenses until it is empty or what remains is deliberate. If `warnings` says the uncategorized lines are unavailable, the lens was still saved.

Pass a fresh UUID `commandId`. After a lost response, retry with the same `commandId` and identical input. The scratchpad has no changes to lens.

targets.description: Select changed lines using repository-relative paths/globs or pinned source ranges. Counts and viewed actions apply only to those lines.

afterId.description: The lens this one follows. Omitted appends.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_rename
tools.description:
Change a Whiteboard session's title. The new title is saved as a new version. The scratchpad's title cannot change.

Pass a fresh UUID `commandId` and your document `leaseId` from `whiteboard_session_activity`; while another agent holds that lease, the rename is refused. After a lost response, retry with the same `commandId` and identical input.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_repin
tools.description:
Replace a Whiteboard session's commit pins or PR identity, keeping its document and component IDs. Use it to attach, replace or detach the session's PR: omitted `pullRequestUrl` keeps it within the same repository and detaches it when the repository changes, a URL replaces it, and null detaches it. To move a session to newer code, prefer `whiteboard_session_set_target`.

`pins` must be full commit IDs from `whiteboard_session_resolve_pins`; the target becomes those commits. Returns `warnings` for source ranges and resources to recheck; fix them with `whiteboard_session_edit`. Earlier pins stay in `whiteboard_session_history`.

Pass a fresh UUID `commandId` and your document `leaseId` from `whiteboard_session_activity`. After a lost response, retry with the same `commandId` and identical input. The scratchpad has no pins.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_restore
tools.description:
Roll a Whiteboard session back to a saved version. Its title, target and pins, PR identity, document and Diff-view lenses from that version are saved as a new version, so later versions stay in history. Find version numbers with `whiteboard_session_history` and read one first with `whiteboard_session_get` and `version`. Viewed progress and Home state are not rolled back. Works on the scratchpad too.

Pass a fresh UUID `commandId` and your document `leaseId` from `whiteboard_session_activity`. After a lost response, retry with the same `commandId` and identical input.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_list
tools.description:
List Whiteboard sessions, to find the `sessionId` of a Whiteboard the user mentions. Each row carries `sessionId`, `title`, `version`, `source` (the target and its resolved pins), `origin` (PR and branch), `repositoryName`, `repositoryPath`, `lenses`, `viewedAt` and `dismissedAt`. Rows carry no document content; read a session with `whiteboard_session_get`. The calling thread's scratchpad is listed (`kind: "scratchpad"`) while the Scratchpad setting is on.

For a pull request you do not need to search: `whiteboard_session_create` with source "pull-request" returns the PR's existing session.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_get
tools.description:
Read a Whiteboard session's document: before editing an existing session, to find component IDs, and to check the whole document before you finish.

The default returns a text outline of every component with its ID and type, abbreviating prose and code. `targetId` returns one component in full; `full: true` returns all content in full. `format: "json"` returns data instead: an ID, type and label list by default, the raw component for `targetId`, or the whole stored version with `full`. `version` reads a saved version from `whiteboard_session_history`; the default is the current one.

Use `whiteboard_session_lens_get` for Diff-view lenses, and `whiteboard_session_source` or `whiteboard_session_file` for code.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_lens_get
tools.description:
Read a Whiteboard session's Diff-view lenses and the changed lines no lens selects yet. Use it before writing lenses and after the last one, to check what remains.

Returns `version`; `lenses` as authored (`id`, `title`, `targets`), each with its resolved `fileCount` and, when it cannot resolve, an `unavailable` reason; and `uncategorized`: the remaining changed lines as `lines` and per-file `files` with `ranges`, plus `moreFiles` when the file list is cut. Group what remains with `whiteboard_session_lens_edit`, and read a file's patch with `whiteboard_session_diff` when the listing is not enough.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_history
tools.description: List a Whiteboard session's saved versions, oldest first, each with `version`, `title` and `createdAt`. Every accepted document, lens, title or target change saves a version. Use it to choose a `version` for `whiteboard_session_get`, `whiteboard_session_restore`, or the `version` input of the source and diff reads.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_open
tools.description:
Show an existing Whiteboard session to the user as a tab in the calling bb thread. Use it when the user wants to see a session that is not open; `whiteboard_session_create` already opens the sessions it creates. It works only when called from a bb thread.

Returns `ok` and `softwareMapEnabled`. Opening changes only what the user sees: it saves no version and needs no lease or `commandId`.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_environment
tools.description:
Check whether the registered checkout behind a Whiteboard session's worktree target can still be read from its bb host. Use it when reads of a worktree session fail and you need to know whether the checkout itself is missing or unreadable.

Returns `issues`: empty when the checkout is readable, otherwise one head-side entry describing the problem. Whiteboard in bb prepares no checkouts of its own, so sessions with a commits target and the scratchpad always return no issues, and `retry` has no effect.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_workspace_cleanup
tools.description: Report Whiteboard-managed checkouts whose removal failed, and retry one by `workspaceId`. Whiteboard in bb manages no checkouts for this tool to clean up: it returns `failures: []`, and any `workspaceId` is rejected as not found. Authoring and reading sessions never need it.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_register_repository
tools.description:
Register a local Git or jj checkout so Whiteboard can read it, and get the `repositoryId` that targets, pins, uploads and explicit-pin reads take. Call it before `whiteboard_session_create` or `whiteboard_session_resolve_pins`.

Pass the checkout's absolute `path` on the calling thread's machine; a path inside the checkout registers its root. Whiteboard binds the repository to that thread's bb host and runs Git there for every later read. Registering the same checkout again returns the same `repositoryId`. A path already registered from another bb host is refused: work on it from a thread on that host, or register a checkout at a different path.

Returns `id` (the `repositoryId`) and `name`.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_resolve_pins
tools.description:
Resolve a base and a head revision (a branch, tag or abbreviated commit) in a registered repository to full commit IDs. Use the result where Whiteboard rejects moving names: source "pins" in `whiteboard_session_create`, `whiteboard_session_repin`, a map upload's `pins`, and `pins` on source references in the document. `whiteboard_session_create` and `whiteboard_session_set_target` resolve a `target` themselves.

Returns `repositoryId`, `base` and `head`. A revision missing from the local checkout fails; fetch it there first.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_upload
tools.description:
Store an image, agent trace or software map for a Whiteboard session to show. Pass a fresh UUID `id` and a registered `repositoryId`, then reference that `id` from a component: `image` `assetId`, `trace_quote` `traceId`, or `software_map` `mapVersionId`.

- "image": one PNG, JPEG or WebP of at most 20 megapixels, as `base64`; it is stored as PNG.
- "trace": a `label` and `events` with unique IDs, for `trace_quote`.
- "map": a software map `model` read at full commit `pins` on one `side`; its source ranges must exist there. Generate maps only when `whiteboard_session_capabilities` reports `softwareMapEnabled`.

Returns `id`, `kind` and `mimeType`. Input is limited to 8 MiB of JSON. Reusing an `id` with identical content returns the same resource; different content is rejected. A session with pins accepts only resources from its own repository, and a map only when its commit on its `side` is the session's commit on that side.

tools.description:
Read an exact line range of code, to verify it before you cite it in a Whiteboard session. Reads the session's current target by default; `version` reads the source a saved version retained, and `commit` reads one commit from `whiteboard_session_commits`.

`source` is `{side, file, fromLine, toLine, pins?}` with a repository-relative `file` and 1-based inclusive lines; this differs from the `start`/`end` source shape in document components. `side` defaults to "head". `source.pins` (`{repositoryId, head, base?}`) reads at explicit commits of any registered repository instead, which the scratchpad needs because it has no pins of its own; a base-side read at explicit pins needs their `base`.

Returns the range with the `commit` it was read at and its `text`. Use `whiteboard_session_file` to read a whole file.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_file
tools.description:
Read a complete source file from a Whiteboard session's current target, for context before you cite ranges from it. `side` ("base" or "head") and a repository-relative `file` are required. `version` reads the source a saved version retained, and `commit` reads one commit from `whiteboard_session_commits`. `repositoryId` and `head` together (plus `base` for the base side) read any registered repository at explicit commits instead, which the scratchpad needs because it has no pins of its own.

Returns `file`, `side`, the `commit` read, and `text`. Binary files are rejected. Use `whiteboard_session_source` for a known range and `whiteboard_session_tree` to find files.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_tree
tools.description:
List the immediate entries of one directory in a Whiteboard session's target, to find files to read. `path` is a repository-relative directory (default: the root) and `side` defaults to "head"; a worktree target includes saved working files. `version` and `commit` select history as in `whiteboard_session_file`, and `repositoryId` and `head` together list any registered repository at explicit commits instead.

Returns entries with `path` and `kind` ("file" or "directory"). Pass a directory's `path` to go deeper.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_diff
tools.description:
Read the change a Whiteboard session shows, before you write about it or group it into lenses.

- `format` "files" (default) lists changed files with `status`, `additions` and `deletions`.
- `format` "patch" returns plain-text patches with base and head line numbers on every line, ready for `review-source:` links. `context` sets context lines; files past `maxBytes` (default 40000, at most 500000) are listed with a `paths:[…]` hint to read next.
- `paths` narrows either format to files or directories.

By default the diff compares the session's base and head. `commit` selects one commit from `whiteboard_session_commits`, `version` reads a saved version's comparison, and `repositoryId`, `base` and `head` compare explicit commits of any registered repository instead. An unexpectedly empty diff usually means a wrong target; fix it with `whiteboard_session_set_target`.

tools.name: whiteboard_session_commits
tools.description: List the commits in a Whiteboard session's comparison, from base to head, each with `commit`, `parentCommit`, `subject`, `author`, `authoredAt`, `fileCount`, `additions` and `deletions`. Use it to walk a multi-commit change one commit at a time: pass a `commit` to `whiteboard_session_diff`, `whiteboard_session_file`, `whiteboard_session_tree` or `whiteboard_session_source`. `version` lists a saved version's comparison.

scratchpadOn.whiteboard_session_get_instructions:
Load Whiteboard's guide before you create or edit a Whiteboard session. A Whiteboard session is a code walkthrough document that the user reads in a Whiteboard panel tab on the calling bb thread. When the user asks for a Whiteboard or to use Whiteboard (for example to review a branch, a change or a pull request, or to explain a system in Whiteboard), call this first and follow what it returns.

TOPICS

- Omit `topic` (or pass "authoring") for the authoring workflow, document structure and component shapes. Read it before `whiteboard_session_create` or your first `whiteboard_session_edit`.
- "file-lenses": how to group a session's changes into Diff-view lenses with `whiteboard_session_lens_edit`. Point the agent that writes lenses to it.

Returns the guide as Markdown.

RULES FOR EVERY WHITEBOARD TOOL

- Read `whiteboard_session_capabilities` before authoring, and generate software maps only when it reports `softwareMapEnabled: true`.
- `whiteboard_session_create` opens the new session as a tab in the calling thread; call `whiteboard_session_open` only to show an existing session.
- Read and write Whiteboard data only through these tools, never through its files or database.
- Every write takes a `commandId` UUID: a fresh one for each operation, and the same one with identical input when you retry after a lost response.

SCRATCHPAD

When the user asks in conversation to be shown how code works or wants a diagram, without asking for a Whiteboard, draw it on this thread's Whiteboard scratchpad instead of answering only in chat. Call `whiteboard_session_capabilities`; if it reports `scratchpadEnabled` and `desktopAvailable`, call `whiteboard_session_get_instructions({topic:"scratchpad"})` and follow it. Session tools address the scratchpad as `sessionId: "scratchpad"`. A request for a Whiteboard, or to use Whiteboard, still means authoring a session with the default topic.
